title: Ukraine says Russia fired 36 ballistic missiles at Kyiv region days before Abu Dhabi talks
dek: Zelensky says Moscow is 'preparing for trilateral talks by launching ballistics'; Russia says it hit a bridge used to move weapons. Both sides have named their teams for Tuesday.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Russia fired 36 ballistic missiles and 172 drones at Ukraine overnight into Saturday, President Volodymyr Zelensky said, damaging Kyiv's Northern Bridge and hitting substations that link two western nuclear power plants to the capital, three days before Russian, Ukrainian and US negotiators are due to meet in Abu Dhabi.

Ukrainian authorities said two people were killed and 37 injured across the country over the past day. Russia's defence ministry said it had struck the bridge because it was used to move weapons for Ukraine's armed forces. Ukraine, for its part, said it had hit a Russian factory that makes missile parts. Neither side's figures can be independently verified.

## What happened

Ukraine's air force said the attack began at 6 pm local time on Friday (9.30 pm IST) and combined Iskander-M, Zircon, North Korean-made KN-23 and S-400 missiles, launched from Russia's Bryansk and Voronezh regions, with 172 attack drones, 137 of them jet-powered. By 9 am on Saturday it said four missiles and 149 drones had been shot down or jammed, that hits were recorded at 24 locations and that debris fell at 10 more. The air force did not say how many missiles were launched; Zelensky put the number at 36 ballistic missiles, all aimed at Kyiv and the surrounding region. The gap between missiles fired and missiles stopped has not been explained by Ukrainian officials.

In Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the roadway, a trolleybus line and a power line on the Northern Bridge across the Dnipro were damaged and the bridge was closed in both directions. Debris damaged a five-storey apartment block in the Solomianskyi district and shattered windows in another, and a two-storey building in the grounds of a kindergarten was badly damaged, city officials said. Klitschko said five people were injured in the city, among them a 14-year-old girl, two of whom were taken to hospital; later counts put the city figure at six. He called the energy situation in the capital "extremely difficult", and the air force said parts of Kyiv lost power, heating and water.

Outside the capital, police in the Kyiv region said one person was killed and two injured; reports said a man hurt when a drone set fire to a house in Bohdanivka, in the Brovary district, later died. One person was killed and 10 injured in the Sumy region, regional officials said, and the governors of the Kherson, Dnipropetrovsk and Donetsk regions reported seven, six and four people injured.

## The power grid and the nuclear plants

Zelensky said "the main target of the strike was again the energy sector". He said Russia hit a substation in the Kyiv region that connects the Rivne and Khmelnytskyi nuclear power plants in western Ukraine to Kyiv and the central regions, and that substations were also damaged in the Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr, Rivne, Kharkiv and Dnipropetrovsk regions. Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal told his German counterpart Katherina Reiche that Russian forces had attacked Ukrainian energy facilities 18 times in 24 hours, according to his ministry.

Zelensky said preliminary forensic findings showed that one key energy facility was hit with KN-23 missiles, "which are manufactured and supplied by North Korea", and that Ukraine still faced "a significant shortage" of interceptors for its US-made Patriot air-defence systems. Neither he nor the energy ministry said whether the nuclear plants had to cut output. The International Atomic Energy Agency, which keeps staff at Ukraine's nuclear plants, had not published an assessment of Saturday's strikes by Saturday evening.

> "Russia is preparing for trilateral talks by launching ballistics at Ukrainian critical infrastructure." (Volodymyr Zelensky)

## What each side says

Zelensky had warned in his address on Friday evening that intelligence showed Russia preparing a new attack on energy infrastructure, bridges over the Dnipro and civilian sites. On Saturday he said Ukraine "must not be left alone" and asked Washington to keep up and increase its support.

Russia's defence ministry confirmed the strike on the Northern Bridge and said it was used to move weapons and military equipment for Ukraine's armed forces. It said its air defences shot down 411 Ukrainian drones overnight; that figure has not been independently verified. Moscow says it targets military and energy facilities used by the Ukrainian army, and denies targeting civilians.

Ukraine's General Staff said its forces had used Neptune missiles to strike JSC Proton-Electrotex in Oryol, which Kyiv says makes components for Iskander-M missiles. Oryol regional officials reported damage to warehouses, production buildings and three houses. A fire broke out at an oil refinery in Saratov after a drone attack, according to reports and Ukrainian monitoring channels, and the Saratov governor, Roman Busargin, said there were preliminary reports of casualties. Kyiv did not formally claim the Saratov strike.

## The Abu Dhabi talks

The attack came as both sides named their teams for the first three-way talks mediated by the United States since February, due on 10 and 11 November in Abu Dhabi. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia's delegation would be led by presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky and include Deputy Foreign Ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov and a senior General Staff officer. President Vladimir Putin met the delegation at a Security Council session on Friday and thanked the UAE for hosting the talks, according to the Kremlin.

Ukraine's delegation will be led by Rustem Umerov, according to Ukrainian officials and reports. Reports said it would also include Kyrylo Budanov, the head of the presidential office; David Arakhamia, who leads the ruling party's group in parliament; and Serhiy Kyslytsia, first deputy head of the presidential office.

US envoy Steve Witkoff has said the talks will cover security guarantees, de-escalation, humanitarian issues and further steps towards a settlement. Some Ukrainian officials have described the round as working-level consultations rather than full negotiations. No ceasefire is in place and neither side has published its proposals.

## Background

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Since 2022 it has repeatedly struck Ukraine's power stations, substations and gas facilities, especially ahead of winter; Ukraine has in turn struck Russian refineries, oil depots and arms factories. This week the United States set out a five-point framework for European security after talks in Brussels with Ukraine, NATO and European governments, and President Donald Trump met a Kremlin envoy at the White House. The Kremlin said on Friday that no European proposals on security guarantees had reached it.

## Why it matters for India

India has called for "dialogue and diplomacy" throughout the war and keeps close ties with both Moscow and Kyiv. It is one of the largest buyers of Russian crude, so any settlement that eases sanctions on Russia would affect what Indian refiners pay and how they pay for it. The talks also matter to the families of Indian nationals still serving with Russian forces, whose release the Ministry of External Affairs says it continues to raise with Moscow. Russia's use of North Korean missiles, if confirmed, adds to concern over arms transfers among sanctioned states. The UAE, the host, is one of India's closest partners in the Gulf.

## What happens next

The Abu Dhabi talks open on Tuesday, 10 November. Road and utility crews were already working on the Northern Bridge on Saturday, Klitschko said. Ukrainian officials had not said by Saturday evening how long repairs to the damaged substations would take.
